title: Internet Gateway and internet egress paths
hook: An Internet Gateway (IGW) is a horizontally scaled VPC edge that allows bidirectional internet traffic for resources with public IPs in public subnets. Without an attached IGW and matching route, even a 'public' subnet cannot reach the internet.

blocks.text: An Internet Gateway attaches to exactly one VPC. It performs network address translation for instances with public IPv4 addresses and routes traffic between the VPC and the public internet. Inbound: internet clients reach instances with public IPs via IGW. Outbound: instances in public subnets with public IPs send return traffic through IGW. Private subnets never route 0.0.0.0/0 directly to IGW — they use NAT Gateway instead for outbound-only paths.

entries.plainDefinition: VPC component enabling internet connectivity for public subnets.
entries.example: Route 0.0.0.0/0 → igw-abc attached to prod VPC.

entries.plainDefinition: Globally routable address assigned to instance or Elastic IP.
entries.example: Auto-assigned public IP on bastion in public subnet.

entries.plainDefinition: IPv6 outbound-only gateway for private subnets.
entries.example: Private subnet IPv6 0.0.0.0/0 → eigw for outbound without inbound.

entries.plainDefinition: IGW is Regional and redundant — not a single physical device you manage.
entries.example: No bandwidth bottleneck on IGW itself — limits are instance/network ACL level.

blocks.text: Every public-facing web tier design starts with IGW + public subnet + ALB. Missing IGW attachment is the first check when 'instance has public IP but no connectivity.' Senior designs minimize instances with public IPs — only ALB, NAT, and bastions (preferably replaced by Systems Manager Session Manager).

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: IGW is VPC edge for public subnets. Inbound to public IP. App tier in private subnet — users hit ALB in public subnet, not EC2 public IP.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

blocks.title: Internet ingress and egress via IGW

items.title: Attach IGW to VPC
items.body: One IGW per VPC needing internet; detached IGW means no internet path.

items.title: Assign public IP or EIP
items.body: Instance or load balancer needs routable address for inbound internet.

items.title: Security controls
items.body: Security groups and network ACLs filter allowed ports — IGW does not replace firewall.

diagram.title: IGW ingress path
diagram.source:
flowchart LR
  Internet((Internet)) --> IGW[Internet Gateway]
  IGW --> ALB[ALB public subnet]
  ALB --> EC2[EC2 private subnet]
  EC2 -->|outbound patch| NAT[NAT Gateway]
  NAT --> IGW

snippet.label: Internet Gateway and public route
snippet.code:
InternetGateway:
  Type: AWS::EC2::InternetGateway
VpcGatewayAttachment:
  Type: AWS::EC2::VPCGatewayAttachment
  Properties:
    VpcId: !Ref AppVpc
    InternetGatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway
PublicRouteTable:
  Type: AWS::EC2::RouteTable
  Properties:
    VpcId: !Ref AppVpc
DefaultPublicRoute:
  Type: AWS::EC2::Route
  DependsOn: VpcGatewayAttachment
  Properties:
    RouteTableId: !Ref PublicRouteTable
    DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
    GatewayId: !Ref InternetGateway
snippet.explanation: DependsOn attachment prevents route creation before IGW is attached — common CloudFormation race.

snippet.label: Verify IGW attachment
snippet.explanation: Empty result means VPC has no internet edge — public subnet routes to igw will black-hole.

snippet.label: Trace route table for subnet
snippet.explanation: Confirm 0.0.0.0/0 targets igw-xxx for public subnet. Private subnet should show nat-xxx or no default route.

sections.heading: Compare with on-premises and C# backends

blocks.title: IGW vs on-prem internet edge
rows: ALB in public subnet → private Kestrel
Reverse proxy in DMZ → internal IIS
NAT Gateway, not IGW on app servers

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Route to IGW without attaching IGW to VPC. Putting application EC2 in public subnet with SSH open to 0.0.0.0/0. Routing private subnet directly to IGW for 'simple outbound' — use NAT. Forgetting DependsOn on CloudFormation IGW route.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: VPC Reachability Analyzer path internet gateway → ALB → target; flow logs on IGW-adjacent subnets showing rejected traffic; avoid public IPs on app tier — use ALB + AWS WAF at edge. IPv6: IGW allows inbound+outbound to instances with IPv6; egress-only IGW for outbound-only private IPv6. IGW itself is not the bottleneck — design for ALB capacity and NAT bandwidth instead.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: ALB cost; must configure target groups correctly
Attack surface — prefer SSM Session Manager
Rejected in security review — no scale or WAF

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Drawing every tier in public subnet with 0.0.0.0/0 → IGW. Strong answer: IGW for ALB/NAT only; users → ALB → private app; outbound private via NAT.

interviewTakeaways: Internet Gateway attaches to VPC and enables bidirectional internet for resources with public IPs in routed public subnets.
Public subnet requires IGW route 0.0.0.0/0; private subnets use NAT for outbound-only internet.
Prefer ALB in public subnet over public IPs on application servers.
60s: IGW = VPC internet edge. Public route + public IP for inbound. App private behind ALB. Outbound private via NAT.
Follow-up: IPv6 IGW versus egress-only IGW?
commonPitfalls: Saying IGW goes on each subnet gets you rejected — one IGW per VPC, route tables point to it.
Strong answer: attach IGW, public RT route, ALB public, app private.
CloudFormation route before IGW attachment — intermittent deploy failure.
Opening SSH 0.0.0.0/0 on app security group because instance is in public subnet.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Node listens on 3000 in private subnet — ALB terminates HTTPS like IIS ARR forwarding to Kestrel on internal port without exposing Node to internet directly.
ALB health check hits /health on private TypeScript API — same pattern as on-prem load balancer probing internal C# service without public IP on app nodes.
